questions.question: Define an invertebrate and state three features shared by all arthropods. Explain why arthropods must moult.
questions.expected_answer: An invertebrate is an animal without a backbone. Arthropods have an exoskeleton (hard outer skeleton of chitin), jointed legs and other jointed appendages, and segmented bodies. The exoskeleton cannot grow, so to increase in size the arthropod must shed it (moult) and expand before the new exoskeleton hardens.

questions.question: Compare insects, arachnids and crustaceans under the headings body parts, legs, antennae and an example.
questions.expected_answer: Insects: three body parts (head, thorax, abdomen); six legs (three pairs); one pair of antennae, often wings; example bee, beetle, mosquito. Arachnids: two body parts (cephalothorax and abdomen); eight legs (four pairs); no antennae and no wings; example spider, scorpion, tick. Crustaceans: usually two body parts; ten or more legs; two pairs of antennae; most breathe with gills in water; example crab, prawn, rock lobster, woodlouse.

questions.question: State three features of molluscs and name the three groups with an example of each. Explain why a crab is not a mollusc.
questions.expected_answer: Molluscs have a soft, unsegmented body; a muscular foot; a mantle that usually makes a shell of calcium carbonate; and often a rasping radula. Gastropods: snail, limpet, perlemoen (one shell or none). Bivalves: mussel, oyster (two hinged shells). Cephalopods: octopus, squid (arms around the head, little or no shell). A crab has jointed legs, an exoskeleton and a segmented body, so it is an arthropod (crustacean), not a mollusc, even though it has a hard covering.
